title: Offload handoff choreography — scratchpad
content:
Context and goal:
- This is a working sketch for how an LLM session (active KV/cache + in-flight tokens) can be offloaded from a hot GPU instance into colder storage or another node with minimal latency penalty and safe resume semantics.
- Motivations: preemption, autoscaling (drain), cross-tier migration (dedicated -> private), edge-snapshotting for client handoff.

Non-goals (for this draft):
- Full encryption key lifecycle (we assume envelope encryption and a KMS exists)
- Billing semantics or quota accounting details (separately tracked)

Key constraints and invariants:
- Resume must be idempotent for replay up to an at-most-once effect model on side effects (functions/calls).
- Handoff should not require global synchronous locks across the fleet; prefer lease + compare-and-commit patterns localized to session owner region.
- Keep hot-path latency impact under 2ms for the typical handoff flow (best-effort; bulk transfer happens async).
- Allow partial resume when only subset of context is available; provide graceful degradation.

Actors and concepts:
- Session owner (hot process): current GPU worker holding KV and token buffers.
- Offload coordinator: lightweight control plane component that orchestrates transfer. Could be colocated with node-agent.
- Target store: object store / S3-like + optional warm worker pre-warming endpoint.
- Resume agent: process on target that claims the session and reconstructs runtime state.
- Lease token: short-lived cryptographic token granting exclusive write/commit rights during handoff.
- Merkle manifest: compact digest of snapshot fragments to validate integrity and support partial fetch/resume.

High-level choreography (happy path):
1) Hot worker notices drain or preemption -> prepare snapshot. Snapshot has two layers:
   - Manifest: small JSON with metadata, fragment list, merkle root hashes, sequence numbers, pinned model version, KV schema version.
   - Fragments: chunked binary blobs (context blocks, tokenizer state, ephemeral caches).
2) Hot worker writes fragments to target store with temporary prefix (e.g., tmp/session-1234/{frag}). Each write returns an upload id.
3) Hot worker computes manifest, including per-fragment upload ids and merkle hashes, and POSTs manifest to Offload coordinator with a request to "commit-offload".
4) Coordinator issues a Lease token (short TTL) and records pre-commit metadata in control-plane KV (idempotent entry: session-1234 -> pending, owner: node-X).
5) Hot worker finalizes manifest commit by calling Coordinator.commit(manifest, lease). Coordinator validates merkle root vs fragment uploads and atomically flips state to "offloaded" and returns resume_endpoint + resume_token.
6) Coordinator makes the object keys immutable (e.g., move from tmp/ to live/ or set ACLs) and notifies target warmers.
7) On resume, resume agent presents resume_token to Coordinator, which validates and issues a short session-level lease for exclusive restoration.
8) Resume agent lazily fetches manifest, verifies merkle root, streams fragments, reconstructs KV/slot state.
9) Once reconstructed, resume agent performs compare-and-swap with Coordinator to claim live session ownership.
10) If success, Coordinator marks session "active" and revokes original owner's lease.

Failure modes and mitigation (notes):
- Partial upload: manifest verification fails -> coordinator rejects commit, hot worker retries with missing fragments.
- Double-commit attempts: Commit flow is idempotent against identical manifest hashes. Use manifest-hash CAS.
- Resume during fragment eviction: include fallback route to request delta pull from originating node if fragments not yet tightened in object store.
- Stale resume token replay: tokens are single-use; store small replay cache keyed by token/hmac.
- Coordinator loss: use control-plane replicated KV (raft/consensus) or less strongly: allow stateless coordinator backed by durable store.

API sketches (very rough) - control plane endpoints and shapes (text sketch):
- POST /offload/request
  body: {"session_id":"s-1234","node_id":"node-x","expected_seq": 987, "snapshot_hint":{"seq_range":"980-987","size_bytes":...}}
  returns: {"upload_prefix":"tmp/s-1234/","upload_urls":[...]}

- POST /offload/commit
  body: {"session_id":"s-1234","manifest_hash":"sha256:...","manifest":"{...}","lease_proof":"sig..."}
  returns: {"status":"accepted","resume_token":"rt-...","live_prefix":"live/s-1234/","resume_endpoint":"worker-claim.example:443"}

- POST /resume/claim
  body: {"session_id":"s-1234","resume_token":"rt-...","requesting_node":"node-y"}
  returns: {"status":"ok","session_lease":"lease-...","restore_plan":"..."}

Lease properties and TTL tuning:
- Keep commit lease TTL small (10-30s), enough for commit handshake but to fail fast on dead workers.
- Resume lease TTL slightly longer (30-120s) to allow reconstruction and small anti-entropy.
- Coordinators should support lease extension RPC guarded by monotonic counters from node to avoid theft.

Merkle/fragment design rationale:
- Merkle allows partial verification (so resume agent can stream only needed fragments and check integrity).
- Fragments should be aligned to semantic boundaries (e.g., tokenizer-chunks, latest prompt delta, recent KV subset) to support partial rehydrate and cost-effective transfer.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want server-side encryption key rotation per fragment? Impacts resume flow.
- How to instrument and surface per-offload cost (bytes, egress) to billing?
- Backup plan for long-tail restores when object-store evicts fragments (pinning vs ephemeral tiering).
- Should we integrate with cache hints from Optimize (e.g., mark fragment hot-score)?
- Interaction with function/tool-calls: if a function was invoked mid-session, we must record idempotency tokens and ensure replays don't double-run side effects.

Quick ASCII diagram (happy path):
  [hot node] --upload--> [object store(tmp)]
      |                          |
      | commit(manifest)         |
      v                          v
  [coord svc] <---record--- [object store(live)]
      |                          |
      | resume_token              |
      v                          v
  [resume node] --fetch--> [object store(live)] --verify--> [resume node runtime]

Notes to self and next steps:
- Prototype small PoC that: captures runtime snapshot (KV + last N tokens) -> writes 4 fragments -> manifest -> coordinator commit -> resume on another local worker. Measure wall-time and latency of resume under different snapshot granularities.
- Add test harness that injects partial uploads, coordinator fail, and resume token replay to validate invariants.
- Document a lightweight client-side library for workers to produce manifest and fragment semantics (python + go prototypes).

Sign-off: rough, needs iteration. Keep this file as the canonical scratchpad until we stabilize API names and move to a proper spec doc.
